clue.text: Edit raunchy writer

parts.note: blue means smutty or risqué, as in a blue joke
a pencil is something you write with

explanation.surface: An instruction to tone down the work of an author of racy material.
explanation.walkthrough: Editors traditionally marked cuts in blue pencil, so the phrase became a verb for censoring or editing.
explanation.definitionFit: To blue-pencil a text is to correct or cut it, an idiom from the editor's coloured marking pencil.

clue.text: Black girl to note, one from La Paz?

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a girl's name
N is the abbreviation for note

explanation.surface: A dark-haired girl writing a letter, perhaps to someone in South America.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks a definition by example: a person from La Paz is one kind of Bolivian.
explanation.definitionFit: La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia, so a native of the city is Bolivian.

clue.text: Relatively expensive in the city bazaar

parts.note: up means in or towards the capital, as in up to town
a bazaar is an oriental market

explanation.surface: Prices at a big city's souk are on the high side.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage you go up to London or up to a university city, so up can mean in the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Upmarket goods aim at wealthier buyers and so cost more than ordinary ones.

clue.text: Exercises with Yanks after medical

indicators.note: after places the word before it second, behind the word that follows

parts.note: a physical is a medical examination
to yank is to jerk

explanation.surface: Americans doing workouts following their health check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yanks' wants to be Americans, but it is a verb for sharp pulls.
explanation.definitionFit: Physical jerks is a jokey British phrase for keep-fit exercises such as press-ups and star jumps.

clue.text: Unfortunate Russian's catching cold in plant

indicators.note: catching means holding something within, so one piece goes inside
an unfortunate person is in a bad way, so the letters are knocked into disorder

parts.note: the word with its s, to be rearranged
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A luckless Russian coming down with a chill while at a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissus is the genus of bulb plants that includes daffodils and jonquils.

clue.text: Sarah's son lives next to a Bill

parts.note: is means exists, lives
taken as written
AC is short for account, a bill

explanation.surface: A woman's boy lodging beside someone called Bill.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Isaac is the son born to Abraham and Sarah in their old age.

clue.text: Ring up over second musical composition

indicators.note: turned over means flipped, so the short word is read the other way

parts.note: a ring is round like the letter O
the word up, flipped
S is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Phoning someone back about a second piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring up' looks like a phrasal verb for phoning, but it splits into a ring and a word that is turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus is the Latin word for work, used for a numbered piece in a composer's catalogue.

clue.text: Quick walk along seafront before gym

parts.note: a prom, short for promenade, is a seaside walkway
PT, physical training, is school gym

explanation.surface: A brisk stroll by the sea before a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: Prompt means done without delay, a synonym of quick as in a quick reply.

clue.text: A Roman god could make it go round

parts.note: it is sex appeal, SA for short
to turn is to rotate, go round

explanation.surface: A deity able to set things spinning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' meaning sex appeal is an old convention; the surface also hints at Saturn's rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn was the Roman god of agriculture and time, identified with the Greek Cronus.

clue.text: Choppy, swelling at end of quay

parts.note: a lump is a swelling on the body

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of quay

explanation.surface: Rough water with a swell breaking at the far end of the harbour wall.
explanation.definitionFit: Lumpy sea is broken and rough, the same sense as choppy water.

clue.text: Think through in study after daughter's left son unconscious

indicators.note: the daughter has left, so her letter departs from the study word

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it
D is the abbreviation for daughter
taken as written
someone knocked out is unconscious

explanation.surface: A family scene: the daughter has gone and the son is asleep over his books.
explanation.walkthrough: D is removed from READ, then the son and the unconscious state follow.
explanation.definitionFit: To reason something out is to work it through logically, a phrasal verb meaning think through.

clue.text: What a saloon bar may serve a saloon car owner, finally?

definitions.text: What a saloon bar may serve a saloon car owner, finally?

parts.words: What a saloon bar may serve a saloon car owner, finally?
parts.note: surface reading: a pub serving a motorist at closing time
setter's reading: a last drink before driving home, the motorist's parting glass

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'saloon' switches between a pub lounge and a car; 'finally' points to the last drink of the night.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom for a final drink before leaving, and road nods to the car owner.

clue.text: Girl, one acting in a servile way in plant

parts.note: a girl's name

parts.words: one acting in a servile way
parts.note: a creeper is a toady who fawns on superiors

explanation.surface: A young woman behaving obsequiously inside a factory or greenhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' could be a factory, but here it is a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia creeper is a climbing vine whose leaves turn red in autumn.

clue.text: Place of great activity in region around the North

indicators.note: one word wraps around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: an area is a region
N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A busy hub somewhere in the north of the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is figuratively any scene of intense activity or conflict, like the political arena.

clue.text: Round of applause in Oval out of place after Surrey's start

indicators.note: letters out of place are disordered and must be rearranged
the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Surrey
the four letters of Oval rearranged

explanation.surface: Cricket fans cheering at the Oval, Surrey's home ground in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is the London cricket ground of Surrey County Cricket Club, which makes the surface a match scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A salvo is a simultaneous discharge of guns, and by extension a sudden burst of clapping.

clue.text: House on the River Lune

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the royal dynasty of the red rose

definitions.note: a description of a place rather than a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the county town of Lancashire stands on this river

explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is a royal dynasty, not a building; the river runs through the Lancashire city.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Lancaster was an English royal dynasty, and Lancaster is also a city on that northern river.

clue.text: Knowing, in one quarter, to provide campaign funds

indicators.note: one element sits in another, wrapped inside it

parts.note: west is one of the four quarters of the compass
arch means knowing or sly, as in an arch look

explanation.surface: Someone in the know in one district raising money for an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A war chest is a fund set aside for a campaign, originally money for a military one.

clue.text: Couple of strikes, disorganized

parts.note: first strike: a slap is a blow with the open hand
second strike: to dash is to strike or smash

explanation.surface: A messy, chaotic pair of industrial stoppages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strikes' suggests walkouts, but they are blows, and two of them are needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Slapdash work is careless and hasty, done in a disorganized way.

clue.text: Boy, James, is given nothing new

parts.note: Jas is the traditional written abbreviation of James
zero, nothing, looks like O
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A boy called James receives nothing novel as a present.
explanation.definitionFit: Jason is a boy's name, so a boy here stands for any given male forename.

clue.text: Advertise opening of trendy bar

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of trendy
a rail is a bar, as in a towel rail

explanation.surface: Publicising the launch night of a fashionable pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be a pub, as the surface suggests, but it is a metal rod.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail a film or programme is to promote it in advance with a preview, hence advertise.

clue.text: Comic strip character, a servant

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the caped crusader of DC comics
second meaning: an army officer's personal servant

explanation.walkthrough: The British army term for an officer's orderly matches the superhero's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The superhero is famous from comics, and in the British army the same word names an officer's attendant.

clue.text: The writer to arouse bit of revulsion

parts.note: to stoke feelings is to arouse them

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small piece, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of revulsion

explanation.surface: An author setting out to provoke a shudder of disgust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The writer' often means the setter, but here it is a specific author whose horror fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Bram Stoker was the Irish novelist who wrote Dracula, so he is the writer meant.

clue.text: A top Etruscan, I am cast in Much Ado About Nothing

indicators.note: metal is cast by melting and reshaping, so these words are remoulded

parts.note: all fifteen letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An ancient Italian actor boasting of being cast in Shakespeare's comedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks theatrical and the title points to Shakespeare, but the play name is a description of fuss over a trifle.
explanation.definitionFit: A storm in a teacup is a great fuss over something trivial, which the Shakespeare title describes exactly.

clue.text: Native to Erin, flower found on top of hill

parts.note: the iris is a flower

indicators.note: in a down entry the top of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of hill

explanation.surface: A wild flower growing on an Irish hilltop.
explanation.definitionFit: Erin is a poetic name for Ireland, so belonging there by birth means being Irish.

clue.text: Get to work on time serving temporarily?

parts.note: to make a place is to get to it, reach it
a shift is a period of work done to a set timetable

explanation.surface: An instruction to arrive at your job punctually.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is loose: a makeshift thing serves only until something better comes.
explanation.definitionFit: Makeshift describes a stopgap that does duty for a while, so it is serving on a provisional basis.

clue.text: Caught in home game, last in series

indicators.note: the letters are trapped inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A batsman out in a home fixture, the final match of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' sounds like cricket, but it signals letters held within words.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the final letter of the Greek alphabet, so it ends a sequence.

clue.text: Habitual grumbler in Noah's first vessel

indicators.note: first means only the opening letter of the name is used

parts.note: the first letter of Noah
Noah's vessel was the ark

explanation.surface: A constant complainer on board the ark.
explanation.walkthrough: Nark is British slang for a moaner (it can also mean a police informer).
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a nark is a persistent complainer, someone who is always griping.

clue.text: Supported Italian child in London district

parts.note: shored up means propped up, supported
It is the abbreviation for Italian
Ch is the abbreviation for child

explanation.surface: An Italian child being looked after somewhere in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoreditch is a district of the East End of London, in the borough of Hackney.
